# Comprehensive Bibliography for OmniPerf-Bench Paper
## Generated by GPT-5 - Complete Citation List

This document contains the full bibliography organized by category, with arXiv IDs, DOIs, venues, and relevance notes.

## Category 1 – AI Coding Agent Benchmarks (Functional Correctness)

### SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?

**Authors:** Carlos E. Jimenez, John Yang, Alexander Wettig, Shunyu Yao, Kexin Pei, Ofir Press, Karthik Narasimhan
**Venue:** ICLR 2024
**arXiv ID:** arXiv:2310.06770
**DOI:** 10.48550/arXiv.2310.06770
**Relevance:** Repository-level benchmark with 2,294 real GitHub issues across 12 Python projects. Closest functional analogue to OmniPerf-Bench for correctness.
**Key metrics:** Claude 2 solves <2% of issues originally.

---

### Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code (HumanEval)

**Authors:** Mark Chen et al.
**Venue:** arXiv preprint, 2021
**arXiv ID:** arXiv:2107.03374
**DOI:** 10.48550/arXiv.2107.03374
**Relevance:** Introduces Codex and HumanEval: 164 hand-written function-level problems. Canonical pass@k benchmark.
**Key metrics:** Codex 28.8% pass@1, 70.2% pass@100; GPT-3 ~0%.

---

### Program Synthesis with Large Language Models (MBPP)

**Authors:** Jacob Austin, Augustus Odena, Maxwell Nye, Maarten Bosma, et al.
**Venue:** arXiv preprint, 2021
**arXiv ID:** arXiv:2108.07732
**DOI:** 10.48550/arXiv.2108.07732
**Relevance:** MBPP: 974 short Python function problems with 3 tests each.
**Key metrics:** ~59-60% on MBPP few-shot, ~10% higher fine-tuned.

---

### Measuring Coding Challenge Competence with APPS

**Authors:** Dan Hendrycks, Steven Basart, Saurav Kadavath, et al.
**Venue:** NeurIPS 2021 Datasets and Benchmarks
**arXiv ID:** arXiv:2105.09938
**DOI:** 10.48550/arXiv.2105.09938
**Relevance:** 10,000 coding problems (intro → competitive difficulty) with 131k test cases.
**Key metrics:** 10k problems, 232k human solutions.

---

### Competition-Level Code Generation with AlphaCode (CodeContests)

**Authors:** Yujia Li, David Choi, Junyoung Chung, et al.
**Venue:** Science 378(6624), 2022
**arXiv ID:** arXiv:2203.07814
**DOI:** 10.1126/science.abq1158
**Relevance:** CodeContests dataset for competitive programming, Codeforces-style problems.
**Key metrics:** AlphaCode median ~top 54% of Codeforces participants.

---

### ClassEval: A Manually-Crafted Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Class-Level Code Generation

**Authors:** Xueying Du, Mingwei Liu, Kaixin Wang, et al.
**Venue:** ICSE 2024
**arXiv ID:** arXiv:2308.01861
**DOI:** 10.48550/arXiv.2308.01861
**Relevance:** 100 class-level Python tasks (410 methods), inter-method dependencies.
**Key metrics:** Models perform substantially worse on class-level vs HumanEval.

---

### CodeXGLUE: A Machine Learning Benchmark Dataset for Code Understanding and Generation

**Authors:** Shuai Lu, Daya Guo, Shuo Ren, et al.
**Venue:** NeurIPS 2021
**arXiv ID:** arXiv:2102.04664
**DOI:** 10.48550/arXiv.2102.04664
**Relevance:** Aggregates 14 datasets across 10 tasks (summarization, translation, completion, defect detection).
**Key metrics:** Multi-task benchmark suite with standard splits.

## Category 2 – Performance-Aware Code Generation

### KernelBench: Can LLMs Write Efficient GPU Kernels?

**Authors:** Anne Ouyang, Simon Guo, Simran Arora, Alex L. Zhang, William Hu, Christopher Ré, Azalia Mirhoseini
**Venue:** ICML 2025
**arXiv ID:** arXiv:2502.10517
**DOI:** 10.48550/arXiv.2502.10517
**Relevance:** 250 PyTorch workloads, LLMs must write correct AND fast GPU kernels.
**Key metrics:** fast_p metric, top models match PyTorch in <20% of cases.

---

### TritonBench: Benchmarking Large Language Model Capabilities for Generating Triton Operators

**Authors:** J. Li, S. Li, Z. Gao, et al.
**Venue:** arXiv preprint, 2025
**arXiv ID:** arXiv:2502.14752
**DOI:** 10.48550/arXiv.2502.14752
**Relevance:** Triton operator generation, correctness + performance on industry GPUs.
**Key metrics:** Strong models miss performance targets without iterative refinement.

---

**Venue:** arXiv preprint, 2025

**DOI:** 10.48550/arXiv.2506.09092

**Key metrics:** 100% / 96% numerically correct on Level-1/2 KernelBench.
